jobs.title: Geological Technician
jobs.description:
We Pursue a Higher Standard

We are a U.S.-based, well-diversified, growing precious metals producer with seven wholly-owned operations: the New Afton gold-copper mine in British Columbia, Canada, the Rainy River gold-silver mine in Ontario, Canada, the Las Chispas silver-gold mine in Sonora, Mexico, the Palmarejo gold-silver mine in Chihuahua, Mexico, the Rochester silver-gold mine in Nevada, the Kensington gold mine in Alaska and the Wharf gold mine in South Dakota. In addition, the Company wholly-owns the Silvertip polymetallic critical minerals exploration project in British Columbia, Canada.

Coeur Alaska’s Kensington mine comprises an underground, hard-rock gold mine, associated milling facilities and a campsite in the historic Berners Bay Mining District, 45 miles north-northwest of Juneau. The mine is accessed via company transportation including bus rides and a boat ride through Lynn Canal.

Coeur Alaska is an integral part of the local community and actively supports education and workforce development programs, environmental stewardship efforts, arts and culture, and local nonprofit agencies through monetary investments, in-kind support, and employee volunteerism.

Approximately 400 miners, mechanics, engineers, operators, geologists, environmental technicians, exploration, and business leaders operate the Kensington mine. Coeur Alaska prioritizes safety, teamwork, career development and growth. If you want to grow your career in a progressive, team-oriented environment, apply today.

About The Job

The Geological Technician will report to the Senior Exploration Geologist and is responsible for various duties related to storage, organization and optimization of core samples. The schedule for this position is 15 days on at the mine site located about 45-miles north of Juneau, accessible only through company transportation, and 13 days off.

Responsibilities

Stop work for safety concerns, and abide by safety best practices, policies and procedures.
Undertake sample handling in the core yard.
Organize core sample transfer to mine lab.
Prepare and load core sample shipments and associated paperwork for transfer to outside labs.
Prepare and maintain records of assay lab submittal sheets and shipment transfer records.
Follow the core sawing requirements for exploration drill holes, as directed by supervisor. 
Help with sample storage efforts.
The successful candidates will work twelve (12) hours per day, fifteen (15) days on / thirteen (13) days off. Position will be located at the camp during shift rotation. 
Perform other duties as assigned

Required Qualifications & Skills

Ability to work safely and promote safe behavior in others.
High school diploma or equivalent.
Positive attitude, strong work ethic, and a team-oriented mindset – being respectful, reliable, and easy to work with is just as important as technical skills.
Willingness to assist others, adapt to changing conditions, and proactively solve problems in a dynamic and inclusive work environment.
Excellent safety, attendance, and work records.
Computer literate (Excel, Word, Outlook).
Comfortable operating heavy equipment (forklifts, skid steer) and light vehicles (pickup truck, flatbed).
Ability to work in multiple-task environment and work with supervisor to properly assign priorities.
Ability to establish credibility and be decisive, but able to recognize and support organization's priorities and preferences.
Ability to work with minimal supervision and communicate clearly (verbally and in writing) with all mine site personnel.
Sets high standards for self and others, builds trust, and takes accountability.

Preferred Qualifications & Skills

Excellent organizational and communication skills. Detail oriented.
Ability to get along with diverse personalities; tactful, mature, flexible and able co-exist in remote camp setting.
Experience with acQuire Database is helpful but not essential.
Preference given to Alaska residents.

Physical Demands

This position requires the ability to safely perform work in a mining environment, including, but not limited to:

Working outdoors in a range of environmental conditions, including rain, snow, ice, wind, cold temperatures, and periods of limited daylight.
Frequent standing and walking on uneven surfaces on surface and underground.
Climbing stairs, ladders, and escapeways.
Lifting and carrying up to 50 pounds often and up to 70 pounds on occasion, pushing and pulling equipment or materials up to 50 pounds, bending, kneeling, crouching, and reaching.
Employees must be able to wear required PPE, including respiratory protection when applicable, work in varying environmental conditions, and participate in emergency response and evacuation procedures.

Mine Site Information

The Kensington Mine is located within the historic Berners Bay Mining District, a region with deep mining roots that date back over a century. The mine site is a remote camp located approximately 45 miles outside of Juneau, Alaska. Transportation to and from the mine site happens twice per day (once in the morning and once in the afternoon) and takes approximately 1.5 hours each way. To get to the mine site, employees board a bus in Juneau that transports to the Yankee Cove dock (~30 minutes), then board a boat (~45 minutes), then board another bus to the camp area (~15 minutes). Food and housing is provided on-site to employees. Rooms are dormitory style with two twin beds, a TV, and storage for your personal belongings.

Notice To Applicants

After submitting your application, you will receive an automated email confirming receipt. Due to a high volume of applications, we are unable to provide individual updates or respond to application inquiries. Only applicants selected for an interview will be contacted.

Many hiring managers work rotational schedules, and the review process may take several weeks. Please note that applicants should not expect additional communication during this time. If you are not selected for an interview, you will receive an email notification once the position has been filled.

Recruitment Window

Applications will be accepted through August 21st, 2026.

jobs.title: Project Solutions Engineer
jobs.description:
Project Solutions Engineer

Location:
Brook Park, OH
Schedule:
Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM-4:30 PM
Why You’ll Love Working With Us

We believe in rewarding hard work and investing in our people. Here are just a few of the benefits we offer:

Fully paid health insurance
We also offer dental, vision, life, and disability coverage
Profit-sharing bonus and team performance bonuses
Fitness reimbursement program
Summer Friday events and team celebrations
Stability from a company that has been in business for over 30 years
Opportunities for growth, learning, and career advancement

About Us:

With over 30 years of industry expertise, our company is a trusted leader in designing and manufacturing pump station packages and controls. We are committed to delivering high-quality service while fostering a culture that values our employees. We offer an excellent benefits package, competitive compensation, and a team-oriented work environment.

Summary:

The Project Solutions Engineer serves as an in-house engineering resource for the Business Development and Project Sales teams, with a focus on reviewing opportunities early, strengthening technical recommendations, and helping move qualified projects from initial review to a clearly scoped, specifiable solution. This role is intended to provide practical engineering judgment, support customer-facing technical credibility, and help give the buyer or specifying engineer confidence in EFG’s design recommendations.

The position supports the BD team by reviewing project information as opportunities come in, commenting on design considerations, identifying risks or gaps, and helping determine whether EFG’s recommended solution is technically appropriate. The role should keep the BD team involved in the customer relationship while reducing the time spent on detailed technical review, design interpretation, and engineering coordination.

For candidates with Professional Engineer licensure, this role may include responsible review and stamping of applicable project work once the individual has developed sufficient familiarity with EFG’s process, standards, products, and internal controls. Use of a professional stamp must be based on sound engineering judgment, proper review, and comfort with the scope of responsibility.

Responsibilities:

Review specifications, drawings, and project data early in the opportunity process to evaluate feasibility, application fit, and technical risk.
Provide practical design comments and engineering recommendations that support BD discussions with buyers, engineers, and project stakeholders.
Help translate customer needs, site conditions, and project requirements into technically sound, cost-conscious system solutions.
Assess hydraulic, civil, electrical, structural, and site-specific considerations to identify concerns before proposals or recommendations are finalized.
Prepare early-stage documentation, including technical summaries, design assumptions, equipment recommendations, review notes, and preliminary layouts.
Prepare design reports, engineering review packages, and supporting documentation for review by external engineers or other qualified reviewers.
Participate in client calls, site visits, pre-bid discussions, and engineer-facing conversations when technical credibility or clarification is needed.
Collaborate with Business Development, Project Sales, internal engineering resources, and external subject matter experts to refine defensible system designs, proposal strategy, and project handoff.
Support responsible engineering review of applicable project work, including stamped work where appropriate based on licensure, review standards, and scope of responsibility.
Maintain current knowledge of EFG products, component manufacturers, industry standards, and application best practices.

Requirements:
Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or related engineering discipline required.
Active Professional Engineer license required or strongly preferred; Civil PE or PE with directly relevant water/wastewater, municipal infrastructure, pump station, or site development experience preferred.
5+ years of relevant experience in civil, water/wastewater, pump station, utility, or infrastructure-related engineering preferred.
Demonstrated ability to review plans, specifications, submittals, and project requirements and provide practical engineering recommendations.
Comfortable working directly with Business Development and Sales teams in a fast-moving opportunity environment.
Ability and willingness, where properly licensed and supported by adequate review, to take professional responsibility for applicable engineering work.
Solid understanding of pumps, hydraulics, site layout considerations, and project design coordination.
Excellent technical writing, communication, and judgment skills.

The Geotechnical Field Technician performs field and laboratory testing in support of geotechnical and construction materials projects under the direction of project managers and senior staff. Performs layout of borings and test pits using conventional surveying techniques and GPS
Observes and classifies soils, test pits, and subsurface conditions
Performs hand auger borings, dynamic cone penetrometer (DCP) testing, and other field investigations

Assists with data reduction and preparation of field and project documentation
Performs field testing, sampling, and inspection of construction materials, including soil, aggregates, concrete, asphalt, masonry, and structural steel
Assists with laboratory testing and sample classification
Communicates daily with contractors, project managers, and team members regarding site conditions and testing activities
Supports preparation of reports, calculations, and documentation as needed
Maintains field equipment and ensures proper documentation of test results
Performs other field, laboratory, or project support tasks as assigned

Required Qualifications

0 years of related experience
High school diploma or GED required

Additional certifications applicable to the work performed may be required

If driving for or on behalf of any ECS subsidiary, a valid driver's license is required
Strong communication skills (verbal and written)
Basic math skills
Ability to read maps, follow directions, and interpret construction plans
Dependable, detail-oriented, and responsible work ethic
Ability to work independently and as part of a team
Ability to safely operate a motor vehicle and comply with safety requirements
Willingness to work in field conditions, including varying weather and site environments

Military Qualifications

The following US Military ranks will qualify for this position IF they also meet the education requirements from the above section titled "Required Qualifications":
E-4

We are employee-owned with more than 3,000 employees in 100+ offices and testing facilities coast to coast. ECS is currently ranked #60 in Engineering News-Record’s Top 500 Design Firms (April 2026), #148 in Engineering News-Record’s Top 200 Environmental Firms (October 2025) and #50 in Zweig Group’s Hot Firm List (May 2025). Function and Scope

The MedAxiom Project Coordinator plays a vital role on the CTS team, providing project coordination, executive administrative, and operational support across various MedAxiom units, including Care Transformation Services (CTS), Revenue Cycle Solutions (RCS), Membership, Marketing, and Ventures.

This role reports directly to the EVP of Care Transformation Services and provides day-to-day project and administrative support. The Project Coordinator will work closely with the lead CTS consultant for each project, partners with teams to coordinate processes and deliver projects on time, within budget, and with desired outcomes aligned with the objectives.

The position serves as a pivotal point of coordination among internal teams, consultants, clients, members, and external stakeholders. Success in this role requires exceptional organizational skills, effective communication abilities, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.

Responsibilities

Coordinate project timelines, milestones, deliverables, and action items across multiple teams, initiatives, and client engagements.
Maintain project plans, task trackers, Monday.com boards, status reports, and project documentation to support organizational priorities and ensure timely completion of deliverables.
Schedule, coordinate, and facilitate meetings, including preparation of agendas, meeting minutes, and follow-up communications.
Monitor project progress, track key deadlines, identify potential risks or barriers, and escalate issues as appropriate to the CTS project lead.
Support the preparation of client deliverables, executive presentations, reports, dashboards, proposals, and other business documents.
Coordinate communications among internal teams, leadership, clients, members, and external stakeholders to ensure alignment and execution of project objectives.
Maintain project files, resource libraries, databases, and shared repositories to ensure information is accurate, organized, and accessible.
Provide administrative support, including calendar management, meeting coordination, travel arrangements, expense reporting, and executive correspondence.

jobs.description:
Description

Is God calling you to ministry?

For over 70 years, The Billy Graham Evangelistic Association (BGEA) has proclaimed the Gospel through its various ministries. Whether you work at our headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina, the Billy Graham Library in Charlotte, North Carolina, the Billy Graham Training Center at the Cove (BGTC) in Asheville, North Carolina, Blue Ridge Broadcasting (BRB) in Asheville, North Carolina or a field office abroad, you are part of a team of committed Christians working together to reach people to the ends of the earth with the Gospel.

Christian Purpose And Expectations

All employees proclaim the Gospel of Jesus Christ through their employment, and thereby further BGEA’s religious mission.

Department Detail – The Billy Graham Rapid Response Team trains and deploys followers of Jesus Christ to minister to the emotional and spiritual needs of those in crisis. Our training equips every-day Christians to know what to say and what not to say when people grieve, and how to compassionately and appropriately share the love and hope found in a personal relationship with Jesus Christ. The Billy Graham Rapid Response Team also deploys crisis-trained chaplains worldwide to offer emotional and spiritual care for those who are suffering or experiencing grief due to man-made and natural disasters. In like manner, the RRT National Law Enforcement Ministry also offers support to men and women facing the emotional and spiritual challenges unique to law enforcement officers and their families.

Job Summary – The Events and Project Coordinator is the liaison between the internal communication department , the Billy Graham Rapid Response Team (BG-RRT) and National Law Enforcement Ministry (NLEM) regarding the completion of all communication projects and other events implemented by BG-RRT and NLEM. This position initiates and ensures the completion of projects surrounding communication plans, print and digital media, websites, and data regarding BG-RRT and NLEM.

Ministry Requirements

Maintains a personal, active relationship with Jesus Christ and is a consistent witness for Jesus Christ
Faithfully upholds BGEA in prayer
Participates in daily BGEA staff devotions including Bible reading, and leading group prayer as schedule permits
Demonstrates behavior aligned with BGEA’s Mission Statement, Statement of Faith, Hallmarks, policies, and expectations
Effectively represents Jesus Christ to those within both personal and professional spheres of influence

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Coordinates print projects for a variety of printed items, posters, banners, credentials, etc., ensuring a reasonable timeline for design, approval, production, and delivery of all print materials and related documentation and approvals
Coordinates various digital projects for BG-RRT events including Sharing Hope in Crisis seminars, Sharing Hope in Jesus’ Name Conference, and Military Chaplain Retreat, ensuring timely delivery of all pieces
Obtains project samples from the internal communication department
Coordinates with Audio Ministry Services (AMS) for all BG-RRT radio needs and ensures proper approvals with appropriate departments
Coordinates with Video Ministry Services (VMS) for all BG-RRT and NLEM video needs and ensures proper approvals with appropriate departments
Serves as a liaison between the internal communications department, specifically with the Digital Content Coordinator and Designer, for all aspects of website creation, design, functionality, and online data collection for all BG-RRT and NLEM events
Initiates requests through Jira Service Management system and coordinates with the Digital Project Manager for all necessary needs pertaining to the BG-RRT database application
Serves as a liaison with the internal communication department, specifically the Digital Writer/Editor, to create practical and attractive email and e-newsletter communication
Initiates email schedule plans with the internal communication department, specifically the Online Content team, for each monthly RRT prayer email and monthly e-newsletter
Serves as a liaison with the internal communication department, specifically the Public Relations and Social Media team, for updating and posting to the BG-RRT and NLEM social media pages for upcoming trainings, deployments, and information about each ministry
Works with Ministry Operations Manager to coordinate domestic and international BG-RRT training events
Coordinates with BG-RRT event speakers/presenters to arrange their travel
Initiates and carries out the creation of Source Codes and Event codes for selects and import requests
Creates, submits, and obtains required approvals for import requests through the JIRA Service Management systemCoordinates with Finance and Inventory Manager to ensure that obsolete materials are discarded and, to the degree possible, old inventory is used before new inventory is ordered
Coordinates with Finance and Inventory Manager to ensure that obsolete materials are discarded and, to the degree possible, old inventory is used before new inventory is ordered

Ensures data obtained from BG-RRT and NLEM events are shared with appropriate departments

Marginal Duties and Responsibilities

Travels to conferences and other BGEA events as instructed
All other duties as assigned

Job Specifications

Skills and Knowledge

Bachelor’s degree with relevant education OR 3+ years of relevant experience
Excellent organizational skills, with high-detail orientation
Excellent computer and software skills, including Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, Jira, and others)
Excellent verbal and written communication skills

Ability to prioritize work effectively to simultaneously fulfill numerous responsibilities, produce under pressure, and meet deadlines
Ability to work productively and independently with minimal direct supervision
Ability to relate professionally with staff at various organizational levels

Physical/Mental Demands

Ability to demonstrate flexibility and adaptability in the midst of changing priorities and circumstances

Working Conditions

Conventional office environment
Extended daily, weekly, and weekend hours are sometimes required
Travel to various RRT conferences and events is required

Mission Statement

Continuing the lifelong work of Billy Graham, the Billy Graham Evangelistic Association exists to support and extend the evangelistic calling and ministry of Franklin Graham by proclaiming the Gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ to all we can by every effective means available to us and by equipping the church and others to do the same.

Statement of Faith

These core beliefs make up the foundation upon which all our ministry endeavors are based.

We believe the Bible to be the inspired, the only infallible, authoritative Word of God revealing the love of God to the world. (1 Thessalonians 2:13; 2 Timothy 3:15-17; John 3:16).
We believe that there is one God, eternally existent in three persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. (Matthew 28:19; John 10:30; Ephesians 4:4-6).
We believe in the deity of the Lord Jesus Christ, in His virgin birth, in His sinless life, in His miracles, in His vicarious and atoning death through His shed blood on the cross, in His bodily resurrection, in His ascension to the right hand of the Father, and in His personal return in power and glory. (Matthew 1:23; John 1:1-4 and 1:29; Acts 1:11 and 2:22-24; Romans 8:34; 1 Corinthians 15:3-4; 2 Corinthians 5:21; Philippians 2:5-11; Hebrews 1:1-4 and 4:15).
We believe that all men everywhere are lost and face the judgment of God, that Jesus Christ is the only way of salvation, and that for the salvation of lost and sinful man, repentance of sin and faith in Jesus Christ results in regeneration by the Holy Spirit. Furthermore, we believe that God will reward the righteous with eternal life in heaven, and that He will banish the unrighteous to everlasting punishment in hell. (Luke 24:46-47; John 14:6; Acts 4:12; Romans 3:23; 2 Corinthians 5:10-11; Ephesians 1:7 and 2:8-9; Titus 3:4-7).
We believe in the present ministry of the Holy Spirit, whose indwelling enables the Christian to live a godly life. (John 3:5-8; Acts 1:8 and 4:31; Romans 8:9; 1 Corinthians 2:14; Galatians 5:16-18; Ephesians 6:12; Colossians 2:6-10).
We believe in the resurrection of both the saved and the lost; the saved unto the resurrection of eternal life and the lost unto the resurrection of damnation and eternal punishment. (1 Corinthians 15:51-57; Revelation 20:11-15).
We believe in the spiritual unity of believers in the Lord Jesus Christ and that all true believers are members of His body, the church. (1 Corinthians 12:12, 27; Ephesians 1:22-23).
We believe that the ministry of evangelism (sharing and proclaiming the message of salvation only possible by grace through faith in Jesus Christ) and discipleship (helping followers of Christ grow up into maturity in Christ) is a responsibility of all followers of Jesus Christ. (Matthew 28:18-20; Acts 1:8; Romans 10:9-15;1 Peter 3:15).
We believe God’s plan for human sexuality is to be expressed only within the context of marriage, that God created man and woman as unique biological persons made for each other. God instituted monogamous marriage between male and female as the foundation of the family and the basic structure of human society. For this reason, we believe that marriage is exclusively the union of one genetic male and one genetic female. (Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:5-6; Mark 10:6-9; Romans 1:26-27; 1 Corinthians 6:9).
We believe that we must dedicate ourselves to prayer, to the service of our Lord, to His authority over our lives, and to the ministry of evangelism. (Matthew 9:35-38; 22:37-39, and 28:18-20; Acts 1:8; Romans 10:9-15 and 12:20-21; Galatians 6:10; Colossians 2:6-10; 1 Peter 3:15).
We believe that human life is sacred from conception to its natural end; and that we must have concern for the physical and spiritual needs of our fellowmen. (Psalm 139:13; Isaiah 49:1; Jeremiah 1:5; Matthew 22:37-39; Romans 12:20-21; Galatians 6:10).
We believe God wonderfully and immutably creates each person a biological male or female. These two distinct, but complementary sexes together reflect the image and likeness of God. Rejection of one’s biological sex is a rejection of God’s merciful design and creative order. (Genesis 1:26-27; Mark 10:6; 1 Corinthians 6:9; Deuteronomy 22:5).

Expectations for Ministry Employment

As An Employee Of Billy Graham Evangelistic Association

I acknowledge that the Lord Jesus Christ is my personal Savior and that I am a personal representative of Him.
I understand that BGEA is a Christian organization whose purpose is proclaiming the message of the Gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ throughout the world.
I agree that the purpose of my employment with BGEA is to further its Christian purpose, that I am prepared to assist in accomplishing that purpose, and that my role with BGEA plays a vital part in carrying out its Christian purpose and mission.
I understand that I must exhibit conduct that is consistent with BGEA’s expectations, whether at work or away from work, in keeping with scriptural teachings and principles as set forth in God’s Word, BGEA’s Statement of Faith, and BGEA’s policies including Christian Conduct.
I understand that BGEA has the right and the responsibility to ensure that its Christian religious purpose is carried on with the highest standards and is not harmed or impeded by conduct that is inconsistent with the Bible, BGEA’s Statement of Faith, its Christian religious purpose, or its policies
I understand that any of my conduct which is not in keeping with the scriptural teachings and principles as set forth in God’s Word, BGEA’s Statement of Faith, and BGEA’s policies, is inconsistent with BGEA’s Chris

The University of Pennsylvania, the largest private employer in Philadelphia, is a world-renowned leader in education, research, and innovation. This historic, Ivy League school consistently ranks among the top 10 universities in the annual U.S. News & World Report survey. Penn has 12 highly-regarded schools that provide opportunities for undergraduate, graduate and continuing education, all influenced by Penn’s distinctive interdisciplinary approach to scholarship and learning. As an employer Penn has been ranked nationally on many occasions with the most recent award from Forbes who named Penn one of America’s Best Large Employers in 2023.

Penn offers a unique working environment within the city of Philadelphia. The University is situated on a beautiful urban campus, with easy access to a range of educational, cultural, and recreational activities. With its historical significance and landmarks, lively cultural offerings, and wide variety of atmospheres, Philadelphia is the perfect place to call home for work and play.

Posted Job Title

Part Time Program Coordinator

Job Profile Title

Coordinator, Program

Job Description Summary

The Department of Family Medicine and Community Health seeks a temporary, part-time Program Coordinator to support the Perinatal Resources for Opioid Use Disorder (PROUD) program during a planned staffing transition. The current Program Coordinator will transition into this temporary role to provide continuity of operations and facilitate the onboarding and training of the incoming full-time Program Coordinator.

The PROUD program is a grant-funded interdisciplinary clinic within Penn Family Care that provides comprehensive clinical care and wraparound services for expectant and postpartum patients with substance use disorders and their newborns. In this temporary role, the incumbent will maintain continuity of essential program operations while transferring program knowledge, workflows, and established processes to the incoming Program Coordinator. Responsibilities include supporting day-to-day grant activities, assisting with clinic operations, maintaining communication with patients and community partners, supporting principal investigators (PIs), completing grant-related reporting requirements, and providing hands-on training to ensure a seamless transition with minimal disruption to program operations.

The position will receive day-to-day direction from the Principal Investigator (PI). This temporary, part-time appointment is intended solely to support the transition of responsibilities and preserve continuity of the PROUD program during the onboarding of the new full-time Program Coordinator.

The federal division of Chugach Alaska Corporation, CGS has been supporting critical missions as a government contractor for over 25 years. Our focus is to support facility maintenance, IT/technical services, construction and education. We are proud to have built, and continue to foster, an incredibly talented team spanning across the globe in hundreds of different fields – each team member proud to serve our country with first-class business services, while also making a difference for our Chugach shareholders.

At CGS, empowering employees is a part of our core, and that focus is one of the ways we build and foster high-performing teams. We empower our employees through competitive compensation and benefits package, professional growth opportunities, truthful communication, and more!

If you are looking for an opportunity to serve something bigger than yourself; if you want your day job to be one that creates meaningful value; if you are looking for an environment that highly values employees and respects individual differences – then Chugach Government Solutions may be the right fit for you!

Position Location

This position is located onsite at the NASA/White Sands Test Facility in Las Cruces, New Mexico.

Job Overview

The IDIQ Project Coordinator provides estimating and coordination assistance in the preparation and execution of all project efforts. The projects managed will be simultaneously requiring strong multi-tasking, monitoring, and tracking skills. The incumbent will also serve as the point of contact for project outages, meetings, and other coordination tasks related to the IDIQ operation. As the Coordinator, they will be responsible for the timely, efficient, cost estimate preparation for the Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) projects assigned to the organization using constructions plans, blueprints, and other associated pricing indexes to include using technicians as subject matter experts in design and estimating for labor and materials.

Responsibilities

Essential Job Duties:

The position duties are facilities design and construction project management including:

Planning, financial management, budget preparation and reporting, field inspection, estimating and multiple project coordination.
Strong verbal and written communication and teaming skills with the ability to handle multiple tasks are needed.
Work under pressure and understand the importance of completing tasks in a timely manner
Work with the customer, NASA facilities personnel as well as other WSTF departments (environmental, safety and mission assurance, propulsion etc) and follow established written procedures a must.
Extensive experience with MS Project software and project management accounting and have experience managing projects utilizing earned value management methodologies.
Receives, performs file setup, and tracks requests for proposal (RFPs), modifications, notices to proceed (NTP) and delivery orders (DO) through receipt, approval, and submittal.
Distribute notifications to all principals throughout the life of a project such as project awards, meetings, outages, etc.
Coordinates pre-bid walk through with all stakeholders.
Reviews, submits, tracks, and distributes requests for information (RFIs).
Reviews proposal packages and other related construction documents for accuracy and content and records data as appropriate.
Develop cover letters, submittal transmissions, and proposal packages to include facilitating submittal to customer.
Assists management team to identify, track, and compile data for key performance indicators.
Generate reports as needed and requested by management team.
Obtains timely quotes and estimates for material, labor, and services required to develop cost proposal.
Analyzes, challenges, and verifies subcontractor quotes and estimates for accuracy.
Works with purchasing team to establish procurement requirements.
Inspects subcontractors and other service providers work to ensure contract compliance, validate labor and material requirements, and facilitate inspection reports.
May attend and assist with final walkouts for scope of work clarifications punch list generation, closeout procedures and satisfactory project acceptance by the government.
Mentors and trains other employees as necessary.
Adheres to the WSTF safety and personnel policies and standard operating procedures.
May be required to work non-standard duty hours and weekends.
Performs other duties as assigned in support of the Facilities department.

Key Responsibilities:

Timely, accurate and efficient performance of job duties.
Harmoniously working with WSTF employees, contractors, and customers.
Providing timely, concise informational updates to project principals.
Experienced in the use of Computerized Maintenance Management Systems, preferably Maximo.
Professional verbal and written communications skills.
Knowledge of construction trade means, methods, equipment, and tools.

Job Requirements

Mandatory:

Position requires a minimum of four (4) years of college or vocational training in area of specialty plus eight (8) years relevant experience, or any equivalent combination of education/experience for a total of twelve (12) years.
Ability to pass pre-hire background and drug screen.
U.S. Citizenship
Valid state driver’s license.

Preferred:

Knowledge and use of Microsoft Project.
Proficient in the use of Maximo CMMS.
College coursework or college degree, preferably in related field.
Previous construction and/or maintenance environment experience.
Ability to read blueprints, drawings, or schematics.
Experience with earned value methodology

Desk/office work and test area work.
Test area work may involve standing and directing technical personnel.
Field work may be necessary. Travel to remote sites/locations may be required.
Walking on uneven terrain including paved areas, gravel/rocks, and dirt/sand is required to access various locations on the facility.
All work must be completed in a safe manner in accordance with NASA and Company safety standards.
Work hours are subject to change, with weekend and/or holiday work as needed. May be required to work outside normal duty hours.

Physical Requirements:

Work is performed primarily in an office setting. This job may involve walking, standing, bending, reaching, and handling items weighing up to 30 pounds.
Work requires the ability to operate a computer, effectively communicate information in verbal and written form, read and review information.
Position is located on a hazardous testing facility; must be able to quickly evacuate buildings in the event of an emergency.
May be required to wear breathing protection (respirator), hearing protection, eye protection and other associated personal protective equipment.

Department Information

California’s Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) brings together the state’s recycling and waste management programs to move the state towards a circular economy that reduces waste and reuses all materials.

Through landmark initiatives like the Integrated Waste Management Act and Beverage Container Recycling and Litter Reduction Act, California works toward a society that uses less, recycles more, and takes resource conservation to higher and higher levels.

CalRecycle’s Mission: Protecting California’s environment and climate for the health and prosperity of future generations through the reduction, reuse and recycling of California resources, environmental education, disaster recovery and the transition from a disposable to a fully circular economy.

CalRecycle values diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. We foster an environment where employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We believe the diversity of our employees is essential to inspiring innovative solutions. Together we further our mission to protect the environment and preserve resources by empowering Californians to reduce, reuse, and recycle. Join CalRecycle to improve the lives of all Californians.

Department Website: http://www.calrecycle.ca.gov

Job Description And Duties

Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory) (EPM I) of the Jurisdiction and Agency Compliance and Enforcement Branch, the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) will oversee a unit within Section One. The unit is responsible for compliance and enforcement related to the Integrated Waste Management Act (AB 939), State Agency and Waste Management Act (AB 75), Mandatory Commercial Recycling law (AB 341), Mandatory Commercial Organics Recycling law (AB 1826), Short-lived Climate Pollutants law (SB 1383), and solid waste laws and regulations in the Public Resources Code (PRC) and California Code of Regulations (CCR). The incumbent will provide first line supervision for Environmental Scientist (ES) staff, applying principles of scientific research, physical and environmental sciences, knowledge of statistical methods or analysis, integrated waste management and industry economics, public health, resource management, assessment, review and analysis of technical documents, review and analysis of operations and monitoring records, inspection of businesses, public agencies, solid waste facilities, and public spaces, and enforcement of AB 939, AB 75, AB 341, AB 1826, and SB 1383. The incumbent will oversee staff’s determination on the significance of violations and their general effect on public health, safety and the environment for the programs; provide oversight, training and mentoring of staff in the determination of compliance with state minimum standards while also providing technical expertise, training and assistance to staff on evaluation and enforcement matters; review findings and reports for technical adequacy; and ensure that enforcement information in the Department’s databases has been accurately input by staff. Additionally, the incumbent will play a key role in the development and implementation of new enforcement programs related to waste diversion laws. The incumbent accomplishes this by: preparing and reviewing environmental documents to determine the effects of proposed activities on the environment; developing regulations and enforcing environmental and state minimum standards; developing recommendations regarding environmental programs; preparing and editing scientific data to develop environmental policies; reviewing business/facility environmental practices; and consulting with and advising other agencies and institutions engaged in related regulation and investigations.

For more information, please see attached the duty statement.

Beginning July 1, 2026, CalRecycle staff will be office-centered, requiring employees to report to the office at least four days per week. About Exponent

Exponent
is the only premium engineering and scientific consulting firm with the depth and breadth of expertise to solve our clients’ most profoundly unique, unprecedented, and urgent challenges.

Our vision is to engage multidisciplinary teams of science, engineering, and regulatory experts to empower clients with solutions that create a safer, healthier, more sustainable world. For over five decades, we've connected the lessons of past failures with tomorrow's solutions to advise clients as they innovate technologically complex products and processes, ensure the safety and health of their users, and address the challenges of sustainability.

Join our team of experts with degrees from top programs at over 500 universities and extensive experience spanning a variety of industries. At Exponent, you’ll contribute to the diverse pool of ideas, talents, backgrounds, and experiences that drives our collaborative teamwork and breakthrough insights. Plus, we help you grow your career through mentoring, sponsorship, and a culture of learning. Thanks for your interest in joining our team!  

Key statistics:

950+ Consultants
640+ Ph.D.s
90+ Disciplines
30+ Offices globally

Our Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Geologist
for our Civil & Structural Engineering
Practice in Los Angeles, CA
or Oakland, CA
. In this role , you will work as part of a team responsible for providing professional services in the areas of engineering geology, remote sensing, GIS, mapping, and geophysics for a range of projects involving the investigation of the cause and extent of failures of geotechnical systems and the evaluation of natural hazards. This position will provide technically challenging work with excellent opportunities to grow within the firm.

You will be responsible for

Conducting field inspections and subsurface explorations (to determine causes of failure of geotechnical systems e.g. slopes, foundations, tunnels, levees, and dams).
Evaluating and characterizing site conditions (for root cause of failure analyses and conceptual mitigation design)
Creation of Geospatial models including GIS and subsurface models
Creation of topographic maps and thematic maps
Assisting with peer review of geologic and geotechnical engineering documents

You Will Have The Following Skills And Qualifications

Ph.D. in g eological s ciences specializing in Engineering Geology or a related field from an accredited university
Alternatively, a M.S. in g eological s ciences specializing in Engineering Geology , or a related field , from an accredited university plus 5 years of experience
Ability to become a licensed professional Geologist (PG) or Geophysicist (PGP) in at least one state within three years
Experience , or related coursework in , Geotechnical Engineering, and Groundwater/Surface Water Hydrology are a strong plus
Demonstrated excellence in coursework and/or fieldwork involving geologic characterization and mapping; experience with geotechnical subsurface investigation techniques a strong plus
Experience with GIS modeling software, graphic software, and imaging software
Ability to gather information from a wide variety of sources (e.g., field investigations, document reviews, and interviews) and to synthetize and convey technical conclusions to individuals in engineering, business, and industry
Strong analytical, field investigation, and critical thinking skills
Attention to detail, dedication to quality and accuracy, desire to work in a fast-paced environment, and effective leadership skills
Strong publication record in peer - reviewed journals or conference proceedings or demonstrated leadership or activity in geologic professional societies, boards, or commissions
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Strong interest in a career primarily involving the investigation of the cause and extent of failures of geotechnical systems and the evaluation of natural hazards

Applicants are encouraged to submit a CV (Curriculum Vitae) with publications (feel free to include publications that are in review or pending) [not restricted to 1 page].

Life @ Exponent

To learn more about life at Exponent and our impact, please visit the following links:

https://www.exponent.com/careers/life-exponent

https://www.exponent.com/company/our-impact

Attracting, inspiring, developing, and rewarding exceptional people with diverse backgrounds and expertise are central to our corporate culture. Our diverse team allows us to provide better value to our clients and enjoy an enriched work environment.

Our firm is committed to offering a variety of programs and resources to support health and well-being. We believe that providing competitive benefits as well as compensation and recognition programs empowers our staff to do work that makes a difference.

Work Environment

At Exponent, we have found that in-person interactions deepen employee engagement and are crucial for development, for realizing the full potential of our talented and diverse teams, and for building a more inclusive workplace where all have a sense of belonging. In our offices, you can expect a supportive culture and a collaborative, dynamic, multi-disciplinary work environment. Our consultants engage in-person in the office unless they are traveling for client work or other business activities.

We value the rich lives our colleagues enjoy outside of work and understand that work/life balance is critical to our employees and their well-being. Consultants have the autonomy to balance their work and personal schedules so you can meet with clients, visit inspection sites, attend conferences, and make time for priorities outside of work, too. It is this flexible, agile work style and working hours that allow our teams to drive innovation and results in their own ways, while meeting the needs of clients.

Compensation

Our consultants are rewarded for their technical and business contributions and have an opportunity to plan for future success and career growth. Exponent's total compensation plan is consistent with its expectations of the quality and quantity of work performed and with the professional standards set by Exponent. At the Associate and Senior Associate level, total compensation includes base salary, bi-weekly bonuses for high-intensity efforts, annual bonus and 401(k) employer contribution of 7% of base salary.

The base salary range for this position is dependent on experience and capabilities which will be assessed during the interview process.

Salary Range

USD $110,000.00 - USD $125,000.00 /Yr.

Benefits You Will Enjoy

Access benefits information on our Life@Exponent page:

https://www.exponent.com/careers/life-exponent

You are the link between inbound deliveries, warehouse execution, and outbound fulfilment. Project Managers rely on you to keep shipments moving, the warehouse team relies on you to give them clear tasks and timely information, and our customers rely on us to deliver on time. WHAT YOU’LL DO:

Work proactively with the Order Management team on inbound ETAs.
Brief the warehouse team before freight arrives.
Create pick tickets and shipment tasks for the warehouse team with everything they need to act.
Physically verify shipments in the warehouse. Parts present, correctly labelled, accurately addressed, nothing missing.
Confirm asset tagging and serial number capture are complete and accurate before anything moves.
Coordinate with the logistics team to ensure shipments are prepared and handed over cleanly for carrier collection.
Follow up with Project Managers for confirmed installation dates. Hardware cannot sit; you push to get delivery dates confirmed and hardware moving.
Escalate storage concerns when project timelines slip and coordinate on-site customer storage options where applicable.
Identify opportunities to receive hardware directly into customer-owned stock, bypassing unnecessary warehouse processing steps.
Maintain accurate records of inbound receipts, warehouse tasks, shipment status, and asset data.
Keep Order Management, the warehouse team, Project Managers, and the logistics team aligned and informed.

A third-level degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Operations, or a related field; 1 to 2 years of experience in a warehouse coordination, logistics, or operations support role; or a combination of relevant work experience and further education such as a post-secondary qualification or professional certification.
Hands-on experience in a warehouse or logistics environment. You are comfortable on the floor, not just behind a screen.
Exceptional attention to detail. You physically verify shipments, check labels, confirm serial numbers, and do not sign off on anything you have not confirmed yourself.
Proactive by default. You anticipate what is coming, prepare the team ahead of time, and flag issues before they become someone else's problem.
Strong communicator across functions. You work daily with warehouse staff, Project Managers, Order Management, and logistics partners.
Organized under pressure. You can manage multiple active shipments simultaneously and keep every task progressing.
Self-starter who takes ownership. If something is not moving, you find out why and fix it.
Comfortable with technology. Warehouse management systems, task boards, and Excel competency expected; additional systems will be trained.

Familiarity with AV, video conferencing, or networking hardware.
Experience with Sage X3, Jira, or similar ERP and project management tooling.
Experience coordinating directly into customer-owned stock or vendor-managed inventory environments.
Track record of improving inbound receipt or outbound fulfilment processes.

new_jobs.title: Senior Geologist (MS/PhD)
new_jobs.description:
About Exponent

Exponent
is the only premium engineering and scientific consulting firm with the depth and breadth of expertise to solve our clients’ most profoundly unique, unprecedented, and urgent challenges.

Our vision is to engage multidisciplinary teams of science, engineering, and regulatory experts to empower clients with solutions that create a safer, healthier, more sustainable world. For over five decades, we've connected the lessons of past failures with tomorrow's solutions to advise clients as they innovate technologically complex products and processes, ensure the safety and health of their users, and address the challenges of sustainability.

Join our team of experts with degrees from top programs at over 500 universities and extensive experience spanning a variety of industries. At Exponent, you’ll contribute to the diverse pool of ideas, talents, backgrounds, and experiences that drives our collaborative teamwork and breakthrough insights. Plus, we help you grow your career through mentoring, sponsorship, and a culture of learning. Thanks for your interest in joining our team!  

Key statistics:

950+ Consultants
640+ Ph.D.s
90+ Disciplines
30+ Offices globally

Our Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Senior Geologist
for our Civil & Structural Engineering
Practice in Los Angeles, CA; Oakland, CA; Bellevue, WA;
or Seattle, WA
.
In this role you will work as part of a team responsible for providing professional services in the areas of engineering geology, remote sensing, GIS, mapping, and geophysics for a range of projects involving the investigation of the cause and extent of failures of geotechnical systems and the evaluation of natural hazards. This position will provide technically challenging work with excellent opportunities to grow within the firm.

You will be responsible for

Conducting field inspections and subsurface explorations (to determine causes of failure of geotechnical systems e.g. slopes, foundations, tunnels, levees, and dams).
Evaluating and characterizing site conditions (for root cause of failure analyses and conceptual mitigation design)
Creation of Geospatial models including GIS and subsurface models
Creation of topographic maps and thematic maps
Assisting with peer review of geologic and geotechnical engineering documents
Evaluating construction claims
Preparation of technical reports

You Will Have The Following Skills And Qualifications

Ph.D. in g eological s ciences specializing in Engineering Geology, or a related field, from an accredited university plus 3 years of experience
Alternatively, a M.S. in geological sciences, specializing in Engineering Geology, or a related field, from an accredited university, plus 5 years of experience
Licensed professional Geologist (PG) or Geophysicist (PGP) in at least one state in at least one state is required
Ability to become a Certified Engineering Geologist (CEG) or Certified Hydrogeologist (CHG) in at least one state
Demonstrated excellence in coursework and/or fieldwork involving geologic characterization and mapping; experience with geotechnical subsurface investigation techniques a strong plus
Ability to work independently or support multiple group projects and to interact with other engineers, scientists, administrative staff, and clients
Degrees, experience, or related coursework in Geotechnical Engineering, and Groundwater/Surface Water Hydrology are a strong plus
Experience with GIS modeling software, graphic software, and imaging software is a strong plus
Ability to gather information from a wide variety of sources (e.g., field investigations, document reviews, and interviews) and to synthetize and convey technical conclusions to individuals in engineering, business, and industry
Strong analytical, field investigation, and critical thinking skills
Attention to detail, dedication to quality and accuracy, desire to work in a fast-paced environment, and effective leadership skills
Strong publication record in peer reviewed journals or conference proceedings or demonstrated leadership or activity in professional societies, boards, or commissions
Record of excellent written and verbal communication skills
Strong interest in a career primarily involving the investigation of the cause and extent of failures of geotechnical systems and the evaluation of natural hazards.

Applicants are encouraged to submit a CV (Curriculum Vitae) with publications (feel free to include publications that are in review or pending) [not restricted to 1 page].

Life @ Exponent

To learn more about life at Exponent and our impact, please visit the following links:

https://www.exponent.com/careers/life-exponent

https://www.exponent.com/company/our-impact

Attracting, inspiring, developing, and rewarding exceptional people with diverse backgrounds and expertise are central to our corporate culture. Our diverse team allows us to provide better value to our clients and enjoy an enriched work environment.

Our firm is committed to offering a variety of programs and resources to support health and well-being. We believe that providing competitive benefits as well as compensation and recognition programs empowers our staff to do work that makes a difference.

Work Environment

At Exponent, we have found that in-person interactions deepen employee engagement and are crucial for development, for realizing the full potential of our talented and diverse teams, and for building a more inclusive workplace where all have a sense of belonging. In our offices, you can expect a supportive culture and a collaborative, dynamic, multi-disciplinary work environment. Our consultants engage in-person in the office unless they are traveling for client work or other business activities.

We value the rich lives our colleagues enjoy outside of work and understand that work/life balance is critical to our employees and their well-being. Consultants have the autonomy to balance their work and personal schedules so you can meet with clients, visit inspection sites, attend conferences, and make time for priorities outside of work, too. It is this flexible, agile work style and working hours that allow our teams to drive innovation and results in their own ways, while meeting the needs of clients.

Compensation

Our consultants are rewarded for their technical and business contributions and have an opportunity to plan for future success and career growth. Exponent's total compensation plan is consistent with its expectations of the quality and quantity of work performed and with the professional standards set by Exponent. At the Associate and Senior Associate level, total compensation includes base salary, bi-weekly bonuses for high-intensity efforts, annual bonus and 401(k) employer contribution of 7% of base salary.

The base salary range for this position is dependent on experience and capabilities which will be assessed during the interview process.

Salary Range

USD $115,000.00 - USD $135,000.00 /Yr.

Benefits You Will Enjoy

Access benefits information on our Life@Exponent page:

https://www.exponent.com/careers/life-exponent

Exponent is a proud equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other protected status.

If you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability, you may email us at HR-Accommodations@exponent.com .

new_jobs.title: PV Solar Field Technician III - McCoy Solar - Blythe, CA
new_jobs.description:
Requisition ID:
96515

NextEra Energy Resources is one of America’s largest wholesale electricity generators, harnessing diverse energy sources to power progress. We deliver tailored energy solutions that fuel economic growth, strengthen communities, and help customers achieve their energy goals. Ready to make a lasting impact? Take the next step in your career with us!

Position Specific Description

The PV Solar & Battery Technician ­­­­will play a crucial role in supporting the operations and maintenance of NextEra Energy's photovoltaic (PV) solar and battery storage systems. As a member of the Operations and Maintenance (O&M) team, the technician will be responsible for ensuring optimal performance and reliability of clean energy systems.

Responsibilities

Conduct routine inspections of PV solar and battery energy storage systems to identify and address any maintenance or performance issues.
Perform preventive and corrective maintenance activities, including cleaning panels, replacing faulty components, and performing tests to ensure optimal system performance.

Please note that this position is based on our campus in Madison, WI, and requires relocation to the area. We recruit nationally and provide financial relocation assistance.

Problem-solving with a purpose.

As a Technical Solutions Engineer at Epic, you’ll work on software that impacts 305 million patients around the world. Alongside customer counterparts, you’ll tackle mission-critical and complex problems – we’re way beyond “turn it off and on again” issues. You’ll need to diagnose the problem, identify a solution, and manage the implementation of the solution, sometimes across multiple physical locations and stakeholders. Learn more about our team at https://careers.epic.com/Jobs/Technical-Solutions-Engineer.

Test the limits of your brain for the most innovative health systems on the planet.

The top-ranked health systems in U.S. News and World Report are Epic customers. Our community includes major systems like the Mayo Clinic, Johns Hopkins, Cleveland Clinic, and Kaiser Permanente, as well as leading academic medical centers at the University of Wisconsin, University of Michigan, University of California, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, and many more.

Live affordably in a city known for its rising tech talent.

Epic is located just outside Madison, Wisconsin, the second fastest growing market for tech talent in the United States and home to the state capital and the University of Wisconsin. Madison, a city surrounded by water, has received accolades for being the greenest city in America (NerdWallet), the best city for renters (SmartAsset), the fittest city in America (Fitbit), and the third best metro in the US for young professionals (Forbes Advisor).

More than just important work
.

Our uniquely themed campus was designed to heighten your ability to get stuff done in your office, a conference room, or by the fireplace in a comfy chair. All meals are restaurant-quality but cost only a few dollars, and they’re prepared by a team comprised of kitchen talent from restaurants around the country. And, after five years here, you’ll earn a four-week sabbatical anywhere in the world. Staff have kayaked in Patagonia, attended a Beyoncé concert in Ireland, built a library in Tanzania, and run a marathon in Antarctica.

We offer comprehensive benefits to keep you healthy and happy as you grow in your life and career, and your merit-based compensation will reflect the impact your work has on the company and our customers. You'll also be eligible for annual raises and bonuses, as well as stock grants, which give you an even greater stake in the success of Epic and our customers. Healthcare is global, and building the best ideas from around the world into Epic software is a point of pride. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we know that inclusive teams design software that supports the delivery of quality care for all patients, so diversity, equity, and inclusion are written into our principles. Please see our full non-discrimination statement at https://careers.epic.com/EEO.

Job Description

Under the direction of the Youth Development Director, the Teen Coordinator is responsible for planning, coordinating, and facilitating engaging, safe, and inclusive programs for teens ages 12–17. This role supports the YMCA's mission by promoting youth development, leadership, academic success, healthy lifestyles, and community engagement. The Teen Coordinator serves as a positive role model, mentor, and advocate for teens while building strong relationships with families, schools, and community partners.

Qualifications

Must be at least 21 years of age.
A minimum of one year working with teens (ages 12-17).
A minimum of six months related program development and/or program management experience.
Previous experience working with diverse populations preferred.
Possess excellent written and verbal communication skills to work cohesively with parents, participants and staff.
Demonstrated computer skills in a Google Workspace

Plan, coordinate, and facilitate engaging, safe, and inclusive teen programs for youth ages 12-17.
Support youth leadership development by mentoring teens, encouraging youth voice, and promoting teamwork, responsibility, and confidence.
Serve as the Lead Advisor for the YMCA's Model United Nations and Youth & Government programs, including weekly meetings, curriculum facilitation, and preparation for conferences, simulations, and civic engagement events.
Ensure the safety and well-being of all participants by following YMCA policies, maintaining appropriate supervision ratios, and implementing positive behavior management strategies.
Host surveys to gauge teen, parent, and community interest. Determine needs of the community to make program decisions.
Plan, develop and implement relevant programs and workshops to engage teen participation.
Build strong relationships with teens, parents/guardians, school staff, and community partners.

Plan and lead Teen Camps for the Santa Monica Family YMCA during Spring/Summer and Mini-Day Camps.

Collaborate with YMCA staff, volunteers, interns, and community partners to support high-quality programming.

Assist in association-wide initiatives such as Healthy Kids Day, Spooktacular, Winter Wonderland and others.
Other duties as assigned.

new_jobs.title: Senior Geologist (MS/PhD)
new_jobs.description:
About Exponent

Exponent
is the only premium engineering and scientific consulting firm with the depth and breadth of expertise to solve our clients’ most profoundly unique, unprecedented, and urgent challenges.

Our vision is to engage multidisciplinary teams of science, engineering, and regulatory experts to empower clients with solutions that create a safer, healthier, more sustainable world. For over five decades, we've connected the lessons of past failures with tomorrow's solutions to advise clients as they innovate technologically complex products and processes, ensure the safety and health of their users, and address the challenges of sustainability.

Join our team of experts with degrees from top programs at over 500 universities and extensive experience spanning a variety of industries. At Exponent, you’ll contribute to the diverse pool of ideas, talents, backgrounds, and experiences that drives our collaborative teamwork and breakthrough insights. Plus, we help you grow your career through mentoring, sponsorship, and a culture of learning. Thanks for your interest in joining our team!  

Key statistics:

950+ Consultants
640+ Ph.D.s
90+ Disciplines
30+ Offices globally

Our Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Senior Geologist
for our Civil & Structural Engineering
Practice in Los Angeles, CA; Oakland, CA; Bellevue, WA;
or Seattle, WA
.
In this role you will work as part of a team responsible for providing professional services in the areas of engineering geology, remote sensing, GIS, mapping, and geophysics for a range of projects involving the investigation of the cause and extent of failures of geotechnical systems and the evaluation of natural hazards. This position will provide technically challenging work with excellent opportunities to grow within the firm.

You will be responsible for

Conducting field inspections and subsurface explorations (to determine causes of failure of geotechnical systems e.g. slopes, foundations, tunnels, levees, and dams).
Evaluating and characterizing site conditions (for root cause of failure analyses and conceptual mitigation design)
Creation of Geospatial models including GIS and subsurface models
Creation of topographic maps and thematic maps
Assisting with peer review of geologic and geotechnical engineering documents
Evaluating construction claims
Preparation of technical reports

You Will Have The Following Skills And Qualifications

Ph.D. in g eological s ciences specializing in Engineering Geology, or a related field, from an accredited university plus 3 years of experience
Alternatively, a M.S. in geological sciences, specializing in Engineering Geology, or a related field, from an accredited university, plus 5 years of experience
Licensed professional Geologist (PG) or Geophysicist (PGP) in at least one state in at least one state is required
Ability to become a Certified Engineering Geologist (CEG) or Certified Hydrogeologist (CHG) in at least one state
Demonstrated excellence in coursework and/or fieldwork involving geologic characterization and mapping; experience with geotechnical subsurface investigation techniques a strong plus
Ability to work independently or support multiple group projects and to interact with other engineers, scientists, administrative staff, and clients
Degrees, experience, or related coursework in Geotechnical Engineering, and Groundwater/Surface Water Hydrology are a strong plus
Experience with GIS modeling software, graphic software, and imaging software is a strong plus
Ability to gather information from a wide variety of sources (e.g., field investigations, document reviews, and interviews) and to synthetize and convey technical conclusions to individuals in engineering, business, and industry
Strong analytical, field investigation, and critical thinking skills
Attention to detail, dedication to quality and accuracy, desire to work in a fast-paced environment, and effective leadership skills
Strong publication record in peer reviewed journals or conference proceedings or demonstrated leadership or activity in professional societies, boards, or commissions
Record of excellent written and verbal communication skills
Strong interest in a career primarily involving the investigation of the cause and extent of failures of geotechnical systems and the evaluation of natural hazards.

Applicants are encouraged to submit a CV (Curriculum Vitae) with publications (feel free to include publications that are in review or pending) [not restricted to 1 page].

Life @ Exponent

To learn more about life at Exponent and our impact, please visit the following links:

https://www.exponent.com/careers/life-exponent

https://www.exponent.com/company/our-impact

Attracting, inspiring, developing, and rewarding exceptional people with diverse backgrounds and expertise are central to our corporate culture. Our diverse team allows us to provide better value to our clients and enjoy an enriched work environment.

Our firm is committed to offering a variety of programs and resources to support health and well-being. We believe that providing competitive benefits as well as compensation and recognition programs empowers our staff to do work that makes a difference.

Work Environment

At Exponent, we have found that in-person interactions deepen employee engagement and are crucial for development, for realizing the full potential of our talented and diverse teams, and for building a more inclusive workplace where all have a sense of belonging. In our offices, you can expect a supportive culture and a collaborative, dynamic, multi-disciplinary work environment. Our consultants engage in-person in the office unless they are traveling for client work or other business activities.

We value the rich lives our colleagues enjoy outside of work and understand that work/life balance is critical to our employees and their well-being. Consultants have the autonomy to balance their work and personal schedules so you can meet with clients, visit inspection sites, attend conferences, and make time for priorities outside of work, too. It is this flexible, agile work style and working hours that allow our teams to drive innovation and results in their own ways, while meeting the needs of clients.

Compensation

Our consultants are rewarded for their technical and business contributions and have an opportunity to plan for future success and career growth. Exponent's total compensation plan is consistent with its expectations of the quality and quantity of work performed and with the professional standards set by Exponent. At the Associate and Senior Associate level, total compensation includes base salary, bi-weekly bonuses for high-intensity efforts, annual bonus and 401(k) employer contribution of 7% of base salary.

The base salary range for this position is dependent on experience and capabilities which will be assessed during the interview process.

Salary Range

USD $115,000.00 - USD $135,000.00 /Yr.

Benefits You Will Enjoy

Access benefits information on our Life@Exponent page:

https://www.exponent.com/careers/life-exponent

Exponent is a proud equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other protected status.

If you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability, you may email us at HR-Accommodations@exponent.com .

new_jobs.title: Technical Solutions Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Please note that this position is based on our campus in Madison, WI, and requires relocation to the area. We recruit nationally and provide financial relocation assistance.

Problem-solving with a purpose.

As a Technical Solutions Engineer at Epic, you’ll work on software that impacts 305 million patients around the world. Alongside customer counterparts, you’ll tackle mission-critical and complex problems – we’re way beyond “turn it off and on again” issues. You’ll need to diagnose the problem, identify a solution, and manage the implementation of the solution, sometimes across multiple physical locations and stakeholders. Learn more about our team at https://careers.epic.com/Jobs/Technical-Solutions-Engineer.

Test the limits of your brain for the most innovative health systems on the planet.

The top-ranked health systems in U.S. News and World Report are Epic customers. Our community includes major systems like the Mayo Clinic, Johns Hopkins, Cleveland Clinic, and Kaiser Permanente, as well as leading academic medical centers at the University of Wisconsin, University of Michigan, University of California, University of Texas, The Ohio State University, and many more.

Live affordably in a city known for its rising tech talent.

Epic is located just outside Madison, Wisconsin, the second fastest growing market for tech talent in the United States and home to the state capital and the University of Wisconsin. Madison, a city surrounded by water, has received accolades for being the greenest city in America (NerdWallet), the best city for renters (SmartAsset), the fittest city in America (Fitbit), and the third best metro in the US for young professionals (Forbes Advisor).

More than just important work
.

Our uniquely themed campus was designed to heighten your ability to get stuff done in your office, a conference room, or by the fireplace in a comfy chair. All meals are restaurant-quality but cost only a few dollars, and they’re prepared by a team comprised of kitchen talent from restaurants around the country. And, after five years here, you’ll earn a four-week sabbatical anywhere in the world. Staff have kayaked in Patagonia, attended a Beyoncé concert in Ireland, built a library in Tanzania, and run a marathon in Antarctica.

We offer comprehensive benefits to keep you healthy and happy as you grow in your life and career, and your merit-based compensation will reflect the impact your work has on the company and our customers. You'll also be eligible for annual raises and bonuses, as well as stock grants, which give you an even greater stake in the success of Epic and our customers. Healthcare is global, and building the best ideas from around the world into Epic software is a point of pride. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we know that inclusive teams design software that supports the delivery of quality care for all patients, so diversity, equity, and inclusion are written into our principles. Please see our full non-discrimination statement at https://careers.epic.com/EEO.

Bachelor's degree or greater
A history of academic excellence or professional success
Willingness to travel occasionally to customer locations
Eligible to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship
Relocation to the Madison, WI area (reimbursed)
COVID-19 vaccination
